title: A novel xylene-free deparaffinization method for the extraction of proteins from human derived formalin-fixed paraffin embedded (FFPE) archival tissue blocks
author: Mansour, Chatila, et al.

steps.title: Collect FFPE tissue blocks
steps.instruction: Obtain the required formalin‑fixed paraffin‑embedded (FFPE) tissue blocks (e.g., 22 human colorectal cancer blocks fixed in 10 % neutral buffered formalin from 2006–2008 and a breast cancer block from March 2014).

steps.title: Deparaffinize tissue with hot water
steps.instruction: Remove paraffin from the FFPE block using hot distilled water instead of xylene and ethanol washes.

substeps.instruction: Place three clean beakers containing distilled water on a temperature‑controlled hot plate and heat until the water reaches approximately 90–95 °C.

When the temperature is reached, place the FFPE tissue block in the first beaker; keep it until the paraffin melts completely and the tissue becomes visible (paraffin wax normally melts around 70 °C).
Transfer the tissue with clean forceps to the second beaker of hot distilled water (90–95 °C) and incubate for 2–3 min.
Finally, transfer the tissue to the third beaker and incubate for another 2–3 min to ensure complete removal of paraffin.

steps.title: Prepare required buffers
steps.instruction: Make all buffers fresh or store aliquots at –20 °C as indicated.

substeps.instruction: Lysis buffer (10 ml): combine 0.5 ml of 1 M Tris–HCl (pH 7.4) to obtain 50 mM Tris–HCl, add 10 µl Triton‑X (1 % stock) for a final 1 % Triton‑X, add 50 mg sodium deoxycholate for a final 0.2 %, add 20 µl of 0.5 M disodium EDTA (1 mM final), add 100 µl of 20 % SDS for a final 0.2 % SDS, and bring the volume to 10 ml with distilled water.
PMSF stock (100 mM): dissolve 174 mg phenylmethylsulfonyl fluoride in 10 ml ethanol, isopropanol, or methanol; store at –20 °C.
2× Laemmli sample buffer (10 ml): mix 1.2 ml of 1 M Tris–HCl (pH 6.8), 4 ml glycerol (50 % v/v), 4 ml 10 % SDS, and 0.8 ml distilled water; store remaining portions at –20 °C.
Fresh homogenization buffer: immediately before use, add 40 µl of the 100 mM PMSF stock to 2 ml of the lysis buffer.

steps.title: Homogenize tissue and prepare protein lysate
steps.instruction: Lyse the deparaffinized tissue and process the extract for SDS‑PAGE.

substeps.instruction: Place approximately 100 mg of the deparaffinized tissue on a clean glass slide kept on ice and cut it into small pieces of about 1 mm³ each.
Transfer the tissue pieces into a clean microcentrifuge tube and add 250 µl of the freshly prepared homogenization buffer.
Homogenize the sample with a homogenizer (or a mini‑homogenizer/sonicator for small pieces) until a uniform solution is obtained.
Transfer the homogenate to a clean Eppendorf tube and heat at 100 °C for 10 min.
Add an equal volume of the 2× Laemmli sample buffer to the heated homogenate.
Add β‑mercaptoethanol to a final concentration of 3 % (v/v).
Incubate the mixture again at 100 °C for 10 min.
Centrifuge the sample at 4000 rpm for 2 min at 4 °C and collect the supernatant containing soluble proteins into a new clean Eppendorf tube.
Measure the total protein concentration of each supernatant sample.
Add bromophenol blue to a final concentration of 0.2 % (w/v).
Load 25 µl of each prepared sample onto an acrylamide gel for mini‑Western blot analysis, or store the remaining sample at –20 °C for later use.

steps.title: Western blot analysis
steps.instruction: Perform Western blot analysis on the loaded gel according to standard procedures.
